title: The Farmer Who Sued the Northern Wind (ZH)
summary: An unreasonable farmer files a lawsuit against the northern wind for blowing down his dry thatch roof. Birbal delivers a comical verdict that restores sanity.
full_text:
A cantankerous farmer named Mangal marched into Emperor Akbar's imperial court in Agra, holding a legal petition scroll. The farmer bowed and declared:

'Your Imperial Majesty! Your laws promise justice against any party that causes property damage in your empire! I demand an imperial summons and arrest warrant issued against the Northern Wind!'

The courtiers stared in disbelief: 'The Northern Wind?'

Mangal yelled: 'Yes! Yesterday afternoon, the Northern Wind blew a violent gust across my village, ripped the dry thatch roof completely off my barn, and scattered my straw across the river! The Wind is guilty of criminal property destruction, and must be fined fifty silver rupees to pay for my roof!'

Akbar was on the verge of throwing the ridiculous farmer out of court, but Birbal stepped in: 'Sire, the law must consider every petition with solemn gravity.'

Birbal addressed the farmer: 'Mangal, your lawsuit is entirely just. The Northern Wind has clearly damaged your property without permission.'

Mangal beamed: 'Thank you, wise minister! Arrest the scoundrel!'

Birbal continued with judicial solemnity:

'However, as you know, imperial law requires that a summons must be served directly into the hands of the accused, and the accused must be brought into this chamber to hear the verdict.

'Therefore, Mangal, the court grants you an imperial arrest warrant!

'You must take this iron cage, go to the northern mountains, capture the Northern Wind inside the cage, seal it with royal wax, and bring the Wind into this court tomorrow morning so that we may sentence it to prison!'

Mangal stood frozen, his jaw dropping: 'How can any man catch the wind in an iron cage?'

Birbal's eyes flashed with triumphant humor:

'Just so, Mangal! If no man can catch the wind in a cage, how can any court command the wind where to blow?

'Nature gives rain, sun, and wind to all creation without favoritism. Instead of wasting your days suing the wind for blowing off a rotten roof, go home, cut sturdy timber, buy good clay tiles, and build a strong roof that can withstand the wind!

'The wise man reinforces his roof; only a fool blames the storm!'

The entire court erupted in laughter. Mangal blushed with shame, apologized for his foolish lawsuit, and returned home to build a proper tiled roof.
